# spdeST

`spdeST` provides proper Matérn SPDE smooths for `mgcv`, finite-element mesh
construction, and covariance score tests for pairs of spatial features. The
SPDE `kappa` is fixed by design and never estimated, so all features share one
Gaussian-process kernel shape and differ only in variance. An intercept is
projected from the SPDE coefficient space before fitting.

Every user-facing `kappa` is unit-scale. The unit length `L` is the largest
per-axis span of the observation coordinates, and `kappa` is the SPDE scale in
coordinates divided by `L`; the package converts it to the mesh scale
internally. The same `kappa` therefore gives the same kernel whether
coordinates are recorded in millimetres or micrometres. Larger `kappa` gives a
more local field. With `alpha = 2`, the practical range is
`sqrt(8 * nu) / kappa` unit lengths, with `nu = 1` in 2D and `nu = 1/2` in 3D.
The default `kappa = 0.05` gives about 57 unit lengths in 2D and 40 in 3D, a
very smooth global field. The examples below use `kappa = 0.1`.

The spatial model of a feature is estimated by `spde.estimate()`, a sparse
Laplace REML fit of the Poisson or negative-binomial SPDE model in compiled
code. `mgcv` builds the fixed-effect design and supplies the smooth
`bs = "spde"`; it does not fit the features.

## Pipeline

The model object from `inlaST.set()` carries every setting that can be fixed
in advance; the `spdeST.*` functions take only the arguments of their own
stage.

```r
model <- inlaST.set(formula, data, family = mgcv::nb(), mesh = mesh)
scan  <- spdeST.scan(Y, model, offset = NULL, adjust = "BY", q.value = 0.05)
fit   <- spdeST.estimate(scan, Y, features = "discoveries")
res   <- spdeST.test(fit, pairs = NULL, moments = "pcalearning")
```

`spdeST.scan()` is Stage 1 (GLM nulls and the SPDE score test),
`spdeST.estimate()` fits the spatial model of the chosen features only, and
`spdeST.test()` tests their pairs.

The package also provides the `mgcv` smooth `bs = "spde"`, which fits the full
projected SPDE basis in `mgcv::gam()`; the fitted-field figures below use it.

Two small spatial-transcriptomics data sets are included: `MISO_E13` and
`Visium_B`. Each contains covariates, three selected genes, a baseline mesh
(`meshes$spde`) and a finer mesh (`meshes$spdePC_g999`, a name kept for
compatibility). Their figures
and results are regenerated when this document is rendered. The final MAGIC
figure is reproduced separately from the larger local data and saved fits.

## Installation

`spdeST` uses CRAN and Bioconductor dependencies; the fitted-field
figures below use `ggplot2`.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("remotes", "BiocManager", "ggplot2"))
BiocManager::install("BiocParallel", ask = FALSE)

remotes::install_github("harryyiheyang/mgcvST", dependencies = TRUE)
```

## Two-step estimation

`spdeST.scan()` fits only the null model of every feature and computes its
Stage 1 null-first p-value (saddlepoint approximation); the p-values are adjusted by `adjust` (`"BY"` by default) into
`diagnostics$marginal_q_value`. `spdeST.estimate()` then fits the spatial
model of the features chosen by `features`: `"discoveries"` (the default; the
Stage 1 discoveries at `q.value`), `"all"`, a vector of feature IDs or indices,
or a logical vector. Stage 1 is not recomputed, and a second call adds
features to an earlier estimate. A null fit keeps no working vector, and the
workers compute the score vector and the mean of the fitted mean
themselves, so the manager holds compact per-feature results only. Features
without a spatial model are marked `spatial_fitted = FALSE` in the
diagnostics, and `pairs = NULL` in `spdeST.test()` tests the pairs among the
features that have one.

```r
scan <- spdeST.scan(Y, model, checkpoint_dir = "estimation-checkpoint")
fit  <- spdeST.estimate(scan, Y)                                  # discoveries
fit  <- spdeST.estimate(fit, Y, features = c("Mapt", "Map1b"))    # add two
fit  <- spdeST.estimate(scan, Y, features = "all")                # every feature
```

With `checkpoint_dir`, each worker saves its chunk when it completes, and a
repeated call resumes from the saved chunks. `Y` must be the matrix given to
`spdeST.scan()`, which is checked.

## WGCNA modules from fitted score covariance

`inlaST.wgcna()` identifies modules within gene blocks selected for downstream
analysis. It accepts a result of `spdeST.estimate()`
and preserves the current fit's score definition, including its nuisance
adjustment. Each block uses the uncentered score covariance `crossprod(A) / q`,
where `q` is the number of selected score coordinates, followed by correlation,
WGCNA adjacency, topological overlap and dynamic tree cutting.

```r
install.packages(c("WGCNA", "dynamicTreeCut", "fastcluster"))

# fit is a result of spdeST.estimate(); genes contains the selected feature IDs.
W <- inlaST.wgcna(fit, indices = genes)
W$modules
W$networks$selected$TOM

# Analyze previously selected blocks separately, preserving their gene order.
W <- inlaST.wgcna(fit, indices = list(block1 = genes1, block2 = genes2), wgcna.para = list(power = 6))
```

The defaults are signed adjacency, power 6, signed TOM, average linkage,
minimum module size 20 and `deepSplit = 1`. A named `wgcna.para` list overrides
only the supplied settings. Module labels are local to each gene
block; label zero indicates an unassigned gene. The result retains score coordinates, covariance,
correlation, adjacency, TOM and the clustering tree for further analysis.

See `help("inlaST.wgcna")` for the interface.

## Model, estimation and pair test

Every spatial field is constrained to average zero over the model
observations.

```r
library(spdeST)
data(MISO_E13, package = "spdeST")
d <- MISO_E13$covariates
basis <- spde_basis(MISO_E13$meshes$spde, as.matrix(d[c("x", "y")]),
                    kappa = 0.1, project_intercept = TRUE)
model <- inlaST.set(
  response ~ offset(offset0) + s(x, y, bs = "spde", xt = basis),
  d, family = mgcv::nb()
)
Y <- t(as.matrix(MISO_E13$expression))
scan <- spdeST.scan(Y, model)
fit <- spdeST.estimate(scan, Y, features = "all")
marginal <- fit$diagnostics[c("feature_id", "marginal_p_value", "marginal_method")]
pairs <- t(combn(rownames(Y), 2L))
result <- spdeST.test(fit, pairs = pairs, moments = "exact")
```

The model of a feature is `y ~ NB2(mu, size)` or Poisson with
`log(mu) = offset + X beta + A u`, `u ~ N(0, (tau Q)^{-1})` under the
mean-zero constraint, with fixed `kappa` and the raw sparse precision `Q`.
`spde.estimate()` maximizes the Laplace REML criterion over the spatial
precision `tau` and the NB size, without a prior on either. The family is
Poisson or negative binomial; the model has one global SPDE field and
fixed-effect nuisance terms, and `inlaST.set()` refuses a model with smooth
nuisance terms or additional random blocks. Controls of the estimator are
supplied as `inlaST.set(..., control = list(spde = list(...)))`, stored in
the model and used by every stage.

The formula may hold the `s(x, y, bs = "spde", xt = basis)` term as above; the
model may also be given as `inlaST.set(formula, data, basis)`, as a prepared
design `inlaST.set(G = gam(..., fit = FALSE))`, or as
`inlaST.set(formula, data, mesh = mesh, kappa = kappa)`, the sparse setup that
forms no dense basis and also takes tetrahedral meshes.

`spdeST.test()` tests each gene pair by the signed
cross-gene score `U = sum(s_i x_i y_i)`, where `s_i` are the singular values of
the product of the square roots of the two score-covariance matrices. The tail
of `U` is a Lugannani-Rice saddlepoint approximation computed in log space on
the `k` leading singular values of a basis shared by all genes, plus a
remainder that matches the remaining power sums of the spectrum, so that
p-values below the double range keep their ordering. The score states are the
reduced observation-kernel states of the sparse score kernel. Two routes
provide the shared basis and the remainder, and the
argument `moments` selects one of them: `"exact"` or `"pcalearning"`. It has no
default; `verbose = TRUE` prints the route and `k`.

* `moments = "exact"` uses the `k = 20` leading eigenvectors of the summed,
  normalized score covariances, the four exact trace moments of every pair, and
  two moment-matched nodes as the remainder. In the 1,025-gene Visium-B
  universe (`q = 298`), the 25,853 pairs of the shared-basis study stay within
  0.0015 of the full-spectrum saddlepoint in `-log10(p)` down to `p = 1e-30`,
  and `k = q` reproduces it. Its cost is cubic in `q` for every pair
  (about 5 ms per pair and thread at `q = 298`).
* `moments = "pcalearning"` projects every score covariance `H_j` onto an
  orthonormal basis of `rank = 100` symmetric matrices learned from training
  genes drawn by stratified sampling on the fitted spatial and observation
  variance scales. Each tested gene is summarized by its basis coefficients
  `c_j`, the two pair traces `tr(H_i H_j)` and `tr((H_i H_j)^2)` come from
  contractions with trace tables computed once, the shared basis holds the
  `k = 80` leading eigenvectors of the training genes, and the remainder is one
  node. On 1,225 held-out pairs of the full-rank MAGIC fit (`q = 1961`), the
  route stays within 0.018 of the full-spectrum saddlepoint at `p = 1e-12`
  and within 0.035 at `p = 1e-20`. Per-gene residuals
  `e_j^2 / ||H_j||_F^2` are returned in `result$pca_learning$genes`. The Gram
  matrix of the training genes is summed in a fixed block order, so one and
  several threads give identical results.

With
`pairs = NULL`, every pair of the available genes is tested in blocks and
streamed to Parquet shards. Each pair is a row of the integer feature indices
`i < j`, `score`, the natural-log two-sided, positive and negative p-values,
the adjusted two-sided `log_q`, `remainder_kind` (0 none, 1 one node, 2 two
nodes, 3 Gaussian) and `status`; feature names are
`result$feature_id[result$results$i]`. The status is 0 for an evaluated pair,
1 or 2 when the kernel cannot give a p-value (the pair then has p = 1 and stays
in the adjustment family) and 3 when a gene has no usable score state (no
p-value, not adjusted). The adjustment (`adjust = "BY"`, `"BH"`, `"Sidak"` or
`"none"`) is applied once to the two-sided family in log space, and positive and
negative discoveries are split by the sign of the score. A `checkpoint_dir`
stores the feature score states, the shared basis and the pair shards under the
algorithm contract `spa_v1`, which records the route, `k`, the remainder order
and the sha of the shared basis; a directory holding pair results from another
contract is refused. The directory records its route, and a resume with another
`moments` stops with a message.

## Included data and observed spatial locations

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "README_files/figure-gfm/"
)

library(mgcv)
library(ggplot2)
library(spdeST)

data(MISO_E13, package = "spdeST")
data(Visium_B, package = "spdeST")

D_miso <- MISO_E13$covariates
D_visium <- Visium_B$covariates

data.frame(
  slice = c("MISO_E13", "Visium_B"),
  spots = c(nrow(D_miso), nrow(D_visium)),
  genes = c(
    paste(names(MISO_E13$expression), collapse = ", "),
    paste(names(Visium_B$expression), collapse = ", ")
  )
)
```

The package stores the original spatial coordinates and expression at each
included spot. The maps below display all observed spots, coloured by the raw
count of one selected gene in each slice.

p_obs_miso <- ggplot2::ggplot(D_miso, ggplot2::aes(x, y)) +

      barwidth = grid::unit(40, "mm"), barheight = grid::unit(2.5, "mm"))
  ) +

    legend.box = "horizontal", plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(6, 16, 6, 6)) +

p_obs_visium <- ggplot2::ggplot(D_visium, ggplot2::aes(x, y)) +

    legend.box = "horizontal", plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(6, 16, 6, 6)) +

grid::grid.newpage()
grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(1, 2)))

grid::popViewport()
```

## MISO E13: SPDE fit, random field, and score test

The following chunk fits `Mapt` and `Map1b` on the MISO mesh. It fixes
the unit-scale `kappa = 0.1`, estimates only the smoothing parameter by REML,
and uses the full projected SPDE basis. For the pairwise test, the raw
`gam(..., fit = FALSE)` setup is prepared by `inlaST.set(G = ...)`.

```{r miso-fit-and-score}
D_miso_mapt <- D_miso
D_miso_map1b <- D_miso
D_miso_mapt$response <- MISO_E13$expression$Mapt
D_miso_map1b$response <- MISO_E13$expression$Map1b
basis_miso <- spde_basis(
  MISO_E13$meshes$spde, as.matrix(D_miso[, c("x", "y")]), kappa = 0.1
)

fit_miso_mapt <- gam(
  response ~ offset(offset0) +
    s(x, y, bs = "spde", xt = basis_miso, sp = -1),
  data = D_miso_mapt, family = nb(link = "log"), method = "REML"
)
fit_miso_map1b <- gam(
  response ~ offset(offset0) +
    s(x, y, bs = "spde", xt = basis_miso, sp = -1),
  data = D_miso_map1b, family = nb(link = "log"), method = "REML"
)

data.frame(
  mesh_vertices = basis_miso$raw_dimension,
  coefficients = ncol(basis_miso$B),
  penalty_rank = as.integer(Matrix::rankMatrix(fit_miso_mapt$smooth[[1L]]$S[[1L]]))
)

G_miso <- gam(
  formula(fit_miso_mapt), data = D_miso_mapt,
  family = nb(link = "log"), method = "REML", fit = FALSE,
  control = gam.control(nthreads = 1L, ncv.threads = 1L)
)
Y_miso_pair <- t(as.matrix(MISO_E13$expression[, c("Mapt", "Map1b")]))
scan_pair_miso <- spdeST.scan(
  Y_miso_pair, inlaST.set(G = G_miso), BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
fit_pair_miso <- spdeST.estimate(
  scan_pair_miso, Y_miso_pair, features = "all", BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
score_miso <- spdeST.test(
  fit_pair_miso, pairs = matrix(c("Mapt", "Map1b"), nrow = 1L),
  adjust = "none", threads = 1L,
  moments = "exact"
)
data.frame(
  pair = "Mapt--Map1b",
  signed_score = score_miso$results$score,
  quadratic_statistic = score_miso$results$score^2,
  log_p_two_sided = score_miso$results$log_p_two_sided,
  p_value = exp(score_miso$results$log_p_two_sided),
  calibration = score_miso$calibration
)
```

The fitted random field is evaluated on a regular grid through the registered
`spde` prediction matrix. Predictions are restricted to the intersection of
the supplied domain and its triangulation, preserving boundaries and holes.

```{r miso-prediction-grid, include=FALSE}
grid_miso <- expand.grid(
  x = seq(min(D_miso$x), max(D_miso$x), length.out = 100L),
  y = seq(min(D_miso$y), max(D_miso$y), length.out = 100L)
)
grid_miso$offset0 <- 0
mesh_miso <- MISO_E13$meshes$spde
loc_miso <- sweep(as.matrix(grid_miso[, c("x", "y")]),
                  2L, mesh_miso$transform$center, "-") / mesh_miso$transform$scale
inside_miso <- !is.na(geometry::tsearchn(
  mesh_miso$mesh$loc[, 1:2], mesh_miso$mesh$graph$tv, loc_miso
)$idx) & lengths(sf::st_within(
  sf::st_as_sf(grid_miso, coords = c("x", "y"),
               crs = sf::st_crs(mesh_miso$domain.original)),
  mesh_miso$domain.original
)) > 0L
grid_miso$field <- NA_real_
grid_miso$field[inside_miso] <- as.numeric(predict(
  fit_miso_mapt, newdata = grid_miso[inside_miso, ],
  type = "terms", terms = fit_miso_mapt$smooth[[1L]]$label
))
```

```{r miso-random-field, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, fig.cap="MISO E13 Mapt fitted SPDE random field, evaluated inside the supplied mesh.", fig.alt="Fitted spatial random field for Mapt in MISO E13, with a horizontal legend below."}
p_miso <- ggplot2::ggplot(grid_miso, ggplot2::aes(x, y)) +
  ggplot2::geom_raster(ggplot2::aes(fill = field), na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_contour(data = grid_miso, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = field),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Spatial field", na.value = "grey85") +
  ggplot2::coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "MISO E13: Mapt fitted random field") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "horizontal") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal",
    title.position = "left", barwidth = grid::unit(70, "mm"),
    barheight = grid::unit(2.5, "mm")),
    colour = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 1))
print(p_miso)
```

## Visium B: SPDE fit, random field, and score test

The Visium example uses the same fixed-`kappa` full-basis construction on
its baseline mesh. Here we test `mt_co3` against `BRAFhuman`.

```{r visium-fit-and-score}
D_visium_mtco3 <- D_visium
D_visium_braf <- D_visium
D_visium_mtco3$response <- Visium_B$expression$mt_co3
D_visium_braf$response <- Visium_B$expression$BRAFhuman
basis_visium <- spde_basis(
  Visium_B$meshes$spde, as.matrix(D_visium[, c("x", "y")]), kappa = 0.1
)

fit_visium_mtco3 <- gam(
  response ~ offset(offset0) +
    s(x, y, bs = "spde", xt = basis_visium, sp = -1),
  data = D_visium_mtco3, family = nb(link = "log"), method = "REML"
)
fit_visium_braf <- gam(
  response ~ offset(offset0) +
    s(x, y, bs = "spde", xt = basis_visium, sp = -1),
  data = D_visium_braf, family = nb(link = "log"), method = "REML"
)

data.frame(
  mesh_vertices = basis_visium$raw_dimension,
  coefficients = ncol(basis_visium$B),
  penalty_rank = as.integer(Matrix::rankMatrix(fit_visium_mtco3$smooth[[1L]]$S[[1L]]))
)

G_visium <- gam(
  formula(fit_visium_mtco3), data = D_visium_mtco3,
  family = nb(link = "log"), method = "REML", fit = FALSE,
  control = gam.control(nthreads = 1L, ncv.threads = 1L)
)
Y_visium_pair <- t(as.matrix(Visium_B$expression[, c("mt_co3", "BRAFhuman")]))
scan_pair_visium <- spdeST.scan(
  Y_visium_pair, inlaST.set(G = G_visium), BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
fit_pair_visium <- spdeST.estimate(
  scan_pair_visium, Y_visium_pair, features = "all", BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
score_visium <- spdeST.test(
  fit_pair_visium, pairs = matrix(c("mt_co3", "BRAFhuman"), nrow = 1L),
  adjust = "none", threads = 1L,
  moments = "exact"
)
data.frame(
  pair = "mt_co3--BRAFhuman",
  signed_score = score_visium$results$score,
  quadratic_statistic = score_visium$results$score^2,
  log_p_two_sided = score_visium$results$log_p_two_sided,
  p_value = exp(score_visium$results$log_p_two_sided),
  calibration = score_visium$calibration
)
```

```{r visium-prediction-grid, include=FALSE}
grid_visium <- expand.grid(
  x = seq(min(D_visium$x), max(D_visium$x), length.out = 100L),
  y = seq(min(D_visium$y), max(D_visium$y), length.out = 100L)
)
grid_visium$offset0 <- 0
mesh_visium <- Visium_B$meshes$spde
loc_visium <- sweep(as.matrix(grid_visium[, c("x", "y")]),
                    2L, mesh_visium$transform$center, "-") / mesh_visium$transform$scale
inside_visium <- !is.na(geometry::tsearchn(
  mesh_visium$mesh$loc[, 1:2], mesh_visium$mesh$graph$tv, loc_visium
)$idx) & lengths(sf::st_within(
  sf::st_as_sf(grid_visium, coords = c("x", "y"),
               crs = sf::st_crs(mesh_visium$domain.original)),
  mesh_visium$domain.original
)) > 0L
grid_visium$field <- NA_real_
grid_visium$field[inside_visium] <- as.numeric(predict(
  fit_visium_mtco3, newdata = grid_visium[inside_visium, ],
  type = "terms", terms = fit_visium_mtco3$smooth[[1L]]$label
))
```

```{r visium-random-field, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Visium B mt_co3 fitted SPDE random field. Grey polygons are the two interior holes excluded by the manual SPDE boundary.", fig.alt="Fitted spatial random field for mt_co3 in Visium B, with two excluded interior holes in grey and a horizontal legend below."}
visium_rings <- sf::st_geometry(
  Visium_B$meshes$spde$domain.original
)[[1L]]
visium_holes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  seq_along(visium_rings[-1L]),
  function(i) data.frame(
    x = visium_rings[[i + 1L]][, 1L],
    y = visium_rings[[i + 1L]][, 2L],
    hole = i
  )
))
p_visium <- ggplot2::ggplot(grid_visium, ggplot2::aes(x, y)) +
  ggplot2::geom_raster(ggplot2::aes(fill = field), na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_contour(data = grid_visium, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = field),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Spatial field", na.value = "grey85") +
  ggplot2::coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic() +
  ggplot2::geom_polygon(
    data = visium_holes,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, group = hole),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.25, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Visium B: mt_co3 fitted random field") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "horizontal") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal",
    title.position = "left", barwidth = grid::unit(70, "mm"),
    barheight = grid::unit(2.5, "mm")),
    colour = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 1))
print(p_visium)
```

## High-throughput baseline-SPDE workflow

`spdeST.estimate()` and `spdeST.test()` retain only the compact summaries
needed for the tested pair universe. Their high-throughput implementation uses
the positive-definite `spde` precision. The following executable chunk fits
all three MISO E13 genes and tests all three pairs (`pairs = NULL` tests every
pair of the available genes); no full `gam` objects are retained after
estimation.

```{r miso-high-throughput}
genes_miso <- c("Mapt", "Map1b", "Hist1h2ao")
D_miso_setup <- D_miso
D_miso_setup$response <- MISO_E13$expression[[genes_miso[1L]]]
basis_miso_full <- spde_basis(
  MISO_E13$meshes$spde, as.matrix(D_miso_setup[, c("x", "y")]), kappa = 0.1
)
G_miso <- gam(
  response ~ offset(offset0) +
    s(x, y, bs = "spde", xt = basis_miso_full, sp = -1),
  data = D_miso_setup, family = nb(link = "log"), method = "REML",
  fit = FALSE, control = gam.control(nthreads = 1L, ncv.threads = 1L)
)
Y_miso <- t(as.matrix(MISO_E13$expression[, genes_miso, drop = FALSE]))

scan_batch_miso <- spdeST.scan(
  Y_miso, inlaST.set(G = G_miso), feature_id = genes_miso,
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
fit_batch_miso <- spdeST.estimate(
  scan_batch_miso, Y_miso, features = "all",
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
test_batch_miso <- spdeST.test(
  fit_batch_miso, pairs = t(combn(genes_miso, 2L)), threads = 1L,
  moments = "exact"
)
cbind(
  feature1 = test_batch_miso$feature_id[test_batch_miso$results$i],
  feature2 = test_batch_miso$feature_id[test_batch_miso$results$j],
  test_batch_miso$results[, c("score", "log_p_two_sided", "log_q")]
)
```

For the packaged three-core versions, set an output directory and source the
two scripts below. Each script writes fit diagnostics, pair results, and
compact R objects to `MGCVST_EXAMPLE_OUTPUT`.

```{r packaged-data-examples, eval=FALSE}
dir.create("spdeST-results", showWarnings = FALSE)
Sys.setenv(
  MGCVST_EXAMPLE_OUTPUT = normalizePath("spdeST-results")
)

source(system.file("examples", "MISO_E13.R", package = "spdeST"))
source(system.file("examples", "Visium_B.R", package = "spdeST"))
```

## Construct a mesh from a boundary

`spde_mesh()` accepts either a manually curated polygon boundary or a boundary
returned by `spde_boundary_learn()`. The example data use curated boundaries.

```{r mesh, eval=FALSE}
loc <- as.matrix(MISO_E13$covariates[, c("x", "y")])
boundary <- spde_boundary_learn(loc, n_holes = 0L)
mesh <- spde_mesh(boundary, loc = loc, target = 150L)
plot(mesh)
```

## Three-dimensional MAGIC example

The mesh setup `inlaST.set(mesh = )` also supports tetrahedral meshes for stacked
sections. The MAGIC example contains 97,830 measured spots on 93 sections,
with their recorded, unequal z spacing retained. Its supplied mesh has
1,962 nodes and 7,676 tetrahedra. Tfap2b is one of the regional markers
displayed in Figure 5d of the [source paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-024-01906-4).

![MAGIC section stack, tetrahedral mesh and three-dimensional fitted Tfap2b
expression, shown as static projections with horizontal legends below.](man/figures/magic-3d-overview.png)

The panels show the observed section stack, the supplied mesh with its
nodes and triangular boundary faces, and fitted Tfap2b expression at the
observed locations. All panels use the same projection and physical scale.
The mesh view shows a cutaway of its original boundary faces (face-centre
x ≤ 4.72 mm), together with all nodes. Expression is displayed as a linear
rate per 10,000 UMI, starting at white for zero and increasing through blue;
values above the 98th percentile (4.62) share the darkest colour.

The fitted expression comes from the saved full-data, spatial-only INLA model
with flat hyperparameter priors and the historical integral constraint.
Section-level random effects remain an ongoing investigation.
